reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address the key premises. E1 describes standard bulk thermal and transport measurements on pellets, not thin-film ultrafast spectroscopy or VDOS modeling. E2 discusses DFT-based electronic transport modeling for a different HEA (PbSnTeSe), with no mention of phonon lifetimes, optical phonon modes, or the proposed experimental-modeling integration. Thus, the specific claims about the mechanism, predictive accuracy, and applicability lack any supporting prior evidence.
premises: Multi-element mass disorder and strain in refractory HEA thin films alter the vibrational spectrum and reduce phonon lifetimes.
Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy can capture these optical phonon modifications and reduced lifetimes.
An advanced VDOS predictive model can accurately model these effects to predict low thermal conductivity.
The combined approach will predict phonon thermal conductivity within ±10%, outperforming traditional models (±20–30%).
The approach is applicable to thin-film refractory HEAs at 300–800 K.
